answer:
Growing rice on this field has a low overall suitability score of 13 out of 100, primarily limited by soil pH and drainage conditions. 

The soil pH is 8.8 (SSURGO soil survey, dominant component of the map unit), which is well above the optimal range of 5.5 to 7 for rice (FAO EcoCrop). Additionally, the field has well-drained soil (SSURGO), whereas rice optimally requires poorly drained, saturated conditions where water is held on the surface for much of the growing season [S1][S2]. 

The climate in Nevada provides only about 63 mm of rain and stored soil water during the growing window (ERA5 reanalysis, 25 km pixel, 2006–2025), falling far short of the optimal 1500 mm to 2000 mm annual rainfall requirement [S1]. While temperature scores reasonably well at an actual 18.7 °C compared to an optimal 20 °C to 30 °C [S1], bridging the massive water deficit through irrigation and managing the high alkalinity would present severe agronomic hurdles.

Consider conducting a soil test to confirm local pH levels before planning alternative crops that tolerate alkaline soils.
